title: Grain Accounting Manual: Grouping the Chargeable Days of a Carry Into Months
content:
How the chargeable days on an unpriced parcel under Grain Marketing Contracts are grouped into months depends on the length of the carry and the size of the parcel.

**Clause 1.** Where the chargeable days reach a whole thirty-day month and the parcel carries at least 1200 bushels, only completed thirty-day months are charged and the part month at the end is dropped.

**Clause 2.** Where the chargeable days fall short of a whole thirty-day month but are not nil, no month is charged at all and the parcel minimum stands as the whole of the charge.

**Clause 3.** Where neither of those holds, the chargeable days are grouped into thirty-day months with any part month counting as a whole one.

## The clauses read against hypothetical figures

| Chargeable days | Bushels the parcel carries | Chargeable months |
|---|---|---|
| 92 | 4,000 | 3, the part month at the end dropped |
| 92 | 1200 | 3, the part month at the end dropped |
| 92 | 1,100 | 4, the part month counting as a whole one |
| 29 | 4,000 | none, the parcel minimum standing as the whole of the charge |
| 29 | 1,100 | none, the parcel minimum standing as the whole of the charge |
| 0 | 4,000 | none |

A parcel of exactly 1200 bushels reaches the parcel month size, so the figure itself qualifies; 1,199 bushels does not. Thirty chargeable days is a whole month, and twenty-nine is not.
